slides.title: Locomotion Variability and User Experience in Smart Wheelchair Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: VARIABILITY-AWARE SHARED CONTROL IN SMART WHEELCHAIRS
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that preserving natural movement variability in shared control for smart wheelchairs increases user agency and usefulness, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Preserving natural human movement variability in smart wheelchair assistance improves user agency and perceived usefulness.
card.key_idea: A shared control strategy using an inverted bell-shaped variability factor to minimize assistance in task-irrelevant regions while maintaining guidance at task-critical start and end points.
card.evaluation: User study with 18 participants pushing an intelligent powered wheelchair; evaluated via ANOVA, trajectory variance, and questionnaires (SoA, QUEAD2, UEQ). Results are statistically significant.

slides.title: D3D-GEN: Robot-Aware Domain-Grounded Interactive 3D World Generation for Social Robotics
slides.tldr: INTERACTIVE 3D WORLD GENERATION FOR SOCIAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: D3D-GEN uses a RAG pipeline to automate the creation of interactive 3D simulation environments, supporting the development of embodied AI for social navigation relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: D3D-GEN generates interactive, robot-aware 3D simulation worlds grounded in autonomously retrieved domain-specific knowledge.
card.key_idea: A RAG pipeline using a domain agent to collect real-world constraints, which then guides LLM-based floorplan generation and semantic asset placement for simulators like Isaac Sim.
card.evaluation: Generated 450 worlds across residential, office, and hospital domains; outperformed baselines (e.g., ProcTHOR, DiffuScene) in object density, visual quality, and VQA accuracy.
card.limitation: Relies on an existing 3D asset database, which may not be available for every target domain.

slides.title: HUI360: A 360° Egocentric Dataset and Baselines for Human-Robot Interaction Anticipation
slides.highlight: This work introduces HUI360, a large-scale 360° egocentric dataset and baselines for anticipating human intentions, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: HUI360 is the largest in-the-wild 360° egocentric dataset for anticipating human-robot physical interactions.
card.key_idea: An automated pipeline using YOLOv11x, SAM2.1, and ViTPose/Sapiens to detect, track, and annotate interactions based on mask intersection with robot zones.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using RF, MLP, and LSTM baselines on HUI360 and SSUP-A datasets via AUC, F1, and AP metrics.
card.limitation: Focuses only on physical contact, ignoring nuanced social cues like gaze, hesitation, or verbal engagement.

slides.title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing
slides.tldr: FRAMEWORK FOR CAPTURING AND TRANSFERRING CONTACT-RICH BATHING DEMONSTRATIONS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for capturing high-fidelity human bathing demonstrations to improve physical human-robot interaction, supporting RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A framework for capturing and transferring high-fidelity human bathing demonstrations to a robot-assisted system.
card.key_idea: Uses contact regions as a processing primitive to reconstruct synchronized motion, shape, and force, enabling retargeting to a tendon-driven soft hand and robotic arm.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a dataset of 128 captures (3 clinicians, 6 subjects) and real-world mannequin tests using L2 distance and tactile pressure metrics.
card.limitation: Significant sim-to-real gap; closed-loop control uses aggregate pressure sums rather than distributions; not yet ready for human subjects.

slides.title: From Speech to Interaction: Analyzing Multimodal Systems in Cocktail-Party Scenarios
slides.tldr: ANALYZING MULTIMODAL SYSTEMS FOR COCKTAIL-PARTY SCENARIOS
slides.highlight: This work analyzes multimodal systems for recognizing speaker groups and transcribing conversations in cocktail-party scenarios, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and diarization.

card.one_liner: Comparative analysis of multimodal systems for speech recognition and conversation grouping in cocktail-party scenarios.
card.key_idea: Evaluates three strategies: audio-visual target speech separation, improved AVSR backbones, and LLM-based semantic clustering to resolve speaker attribution and interaction structure.
card.evaluation: Tested on CHiME-9 MCoRec dataset using WER, Clustering F1, and JointError; LLM-based clustering and robust AVSR showed the best results.
card.limitation: Systems remain modular rather than end-to-end; semantic clustering depends on transcription quality, and visual cues generalize poorly.

slides.title: Enhancing Virtual Agents through SLMs and Edge-Computing: An Exploratory Evaluation of Think and Memory Processes
slides.tldr: EDGE-BASED SLM FRAMEWORK FOR VIRTUAL AGENTS
slides.highlight: This research explores using Small Language Models (SLMs) and edge computing to implement cognitive processes like thinking and memory for embodied virtual agents. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated interaction.

card.one_liner: Explores using Small Language Models (SLMs) on edge hardware to power cognitive processes for virtual agents.
card.key_idea: Implements the 'Think' (service routing) and 'Memory' (fact extraction/retrieval) components of the CEAA framework using Qwen2.5 SLMs on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX.
card.evaluation: Tested 0.5B, 1.5B, and 3.0B models via 1,000 routing prompts and 250 memory pairs; 3.0B model showed highest accuracy but highest latency.
card.limitation: Conducted in a controlled test-bed without live 3D interaction; limited to one hardware configuration and three model variants.

slides.title: X Square Robot's HOST Learns from Short Videos
slides.highlight: X Square Robot's HOST demonstrates the ability to learn from short videos, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied learning.

slides.title: FlowLOB: Efficient and Controllable Limit Order Book Generation with Flow Matching
slides.tldr: EFFICIENT LIMIT ORDER BOOK GENERATION VIA FLOW MATCHING
slides.highlight: FlowLOB utilizes flow-matching to generate realistic and controllable limit order book trajectories, providing a method for simulating complex market dynamics relevant to MIMIC's societal-scale simulation goals.

card.one_liner: FlowLOB uses flow matching to generate realistic, controllable limit order book trajectories with high sampling efficiency.
card.key_idea: A conditional flow-matching generator using an adaLN-Zero transformer and tick-relative representation to enable multi-symbol training and zero-shot transfer to unseen instruments.
card.evaluation: Tested on HKEX symbols using Wasserstein-1, KS, KL, and JS metrics against agent-based and learned baselines; results show superior realism at high frequencies.
card.limitation: Performance and controllability degrade at coarser sampling frequencies (10s), where it no longer dominates marginal distributional metrics.

slides.title: Booster Robotics Unveils Booster T2 Humanoid Platform
slides.tldr: NEW HUMANOID PLATFORM FOR EMBODIED AI
slides.highlight: The Booster T2 platform provides a humanoid system for embodied AI development, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.
